findings.issue: ScanAsync (line 392) always overwrites the dialog's sentence with CoreAr.Documents.ScanPagesDone(scan.Pages.Count), so a scan whose bytes could NOT be stored still reports success. If the vault goes out of reach between the scan and the store (a drive unplugged — exactly the «الخزنة غير متاحة» case this package exists to handle), StoreAsync returns DocumentImportState.VaultUnavailable with VaultUnavailableMessage, and ScanAsync throws that sentence away: the office is told «تم مسح صفحة واحدة.» while ScanState is Ok and nothing was saved. The same return also hides partial loss in the separate-pages branch (lines 376-387), where the results of pages 2..n are discarded entirely — if the vault fails after page 1, the message still counts every sheet. No test covers a scan against an unavailable vault.
findings.fix: After the store, branch on the import before composing the sentence: `if (import is not null && !import.IsStored) { return new DocumentScanImport(scan.State, import, scan.Pages.Count, import.MessageAr); }` so the vault's own «لم نتمكّن من الوصول إلى مكان حفظ الملفات الأصلية…» reaches W45. In the separate-pages branch keep the results of the loop (e.g. `var stored = 1; ... if (!page.IsStored) return new DocumentScanImport(scan.State, page, scan.Pages.Count, page.MessageAr); stored++;`) and report ScanPagesDone(stored) rather than scan.Pages.Count. Add a test: a DocumentsWorld whose vault folder is replaced by a file (as VaultStoreTests.A_vault_whose_folder_cannot_be_made_refuses_the_write_instead_of_pretending does) plus a FakeScanner, asserting !result.IsStored and result.MessageAr == CoreAr.Documents.VaultUnavailableMessage.

findings.issue: CheckHash (line 414) validates only that the name is 64 characters long, not that it is hexadecimal. Every path is then built as Path.Combine(VaultDir, hash[..2], hash + ".bin"), so a 64-character value containing separators (e.g. a documents row arriving from another device through B4 sync) resolves outside vault\ and is probed by File.Exists; and because SubKey's Convert.FromHexString runs only after that probe, a malformed name leaves the store with an unhandled FormatException instead of the clean states the interface promises.
findings.fix: In CheckHash also require hex: `if (sha256Hex.Length != 64 || !sha256Hex.All(Uri.IsHexDigit)) throw new ArgumentException("A vault file is named by a 64 character SHA-256 hex string.", nameof(sha256Hex));`. Add a case to A_hash_that_is_not_a_hash_is_a_defect_and_not_a_state covering a 64-character non-hex value with a path separator in it.

findings.issue: ReadName (line 488) releases its COM wrappers only on the success paths: if dynamicName.get_Value() throws (a driver whose Name property is not a string), both `nameProperty` and `properties` are left to the finalizer, which is the same leak round 1's finding 4 fixed in FindDevice — and ReadName is called once per enumerated device, so it is on the device-list path the office uses every time W45 opens.
findings.fix: Restructure ReadName like ReadProperty: declare `object? properties = null; object? nameProperty = null;` outside the try and release both in a finally, returning the id from the single exit.

findings.issue: ReadAsync (line 89) passes the token to Task.Run, so when the token is already cancelled at the moment the work is scheduled the task faults with TaskCanceledException instead of returning OcrState.Cancelled. OcrQueue.ReadCoreAsync has by then already written OcrStatus.Running (OcrQueue.cs line 290), so the exception escapes DrainAsync and the document stays «جارٍ قراءة النص» until the next ResumeAsync — the one shape of a cut-off run that round 1's finding 1 did not close.
findings.fix: Drop the token from the Task.Run overload (`Task.Run(() => Read(content, mediaType, progress, cancellationToken))`); Read already turns cancellation into OcrState.Cancelled with its finished pages, which is what the queue is written to handle.

findings.issue: ResumeAsync (lines 145-154) calls the Pending property twice per document to decide whether Enqueue added anything; each call takes the lock, projects and sorts the whole waiting list, so resuming after a restore that left a few thousand documents pending is quadratic with a lock per step, on the path that runs when a session opens.
findings.fix: Have Enqueue report what it did — e.g. change it to a private bool TryEnqueue(Guid, OcrPriority) that returns true when it added an entry, with the public void Enqueue calling it — and count that return value instead of comparing Pending.Count.

missing_spec_items: Nothing in the product ever starts the queue: IOcrQueue.ResumeAsync and DrainAsync have no caller anywhere under src/ outside Wakeel.Ocr itself (verified by grep). The queue is registered, resumes correctly and is covered by tests, but until a session-open resume and an idle-pass drain are wired, no document's text is ever read in the running application. The builder documented this as belonging to B3-2b, together with the warning that OcrQueue is Scoped over the session's WakeelDb (shared with the Blazor UI), so the drain must run in its own scope; it needs assigning explicitly.

ROUND 1 FINDINGS — all nine verified fixed in the code, not just claimed. (1) OcrQueue.ReadCoreAsync lines 298-314 keeps a cancelled run's pages and re-marks Pending, both writes on CancellationToken.None, with the zero-page branch handled too; test A_document_stopped_halfway_keeps_its_pages_and_stays_in_line drives a real cancellation at page 3 of 20 and then proves a fresh queue finishes it to 20. (2) DocumentService.ActorAsync (line 785) mirrors CorrespondenceService; grep finds no literal \"system\" left in Services/Documents; test asserts the audit Actor equals Installation.EmployeeName. (3) ScanAsync guards on `_scanner is null` alone; FakeScanner now models the real cached probe (HasDevice vs _saw), and Scanning_before_the_device_list_was_ever_asked_for_still_scans fails on the old guard. (4) FindDevice's keep/finally releases both continue paths. (5) Fingerprint folds LastWriteTimeUtc.Ticks; the same-size-replacement test is real. (6) The walk-up candidate is gated on Wakeel.slnx and the tests still resolve tools/tessdata. (7) ScanPdfWriter counts written pages and throws; ScanAsync binds first and falls through, with two tests including one through the real Skia writer. (8) _done/_total are incremented and read as a pair under _gate. (9) The XML doc is rewritten.

SECURITY. Originals are hashed before encryption and filed at vault\\ab\\<sha>.bin; each file is sealed with an HKDF sub key over the vault key salted with the file's own hash, label \"wakeel.vault.file\"; the sealed form is Aead.EncryptStream's chunked frames with the hash as associated data, so a file cannot be moved to another hash's name (test A_file_moved_to_another_hashs_name_reads_as_corrupt). Writes go to a GUID temporary and are File.Move'd with overwrite:false, with the temporary deleted on every failure path. Reads verify twice — the AEAD tag and then the SHA-256 of the plaintext — and a corrupt read returns no bytes (tamper, truncation and cross-filing all tested). The vault key is fetched per call and zeroed in a finally; SessionVaultKeyProvider keeps no copy. No OCR path ever writes plaintext to disk: PdfRasterizer hands PNG bytes straight to Pix.LoadFromMemory. Size and kind are both enforced before the bytes are read (ImportFileAsync checks FileInfo.Length first) and the name and the magic bytes must agree. Reading is CPU work on the thread pool and the drain yields between documents.

ARABIC/RTL. All user-facing text is in CoreAr.Documents (now a partial-class file per the supervisor's ruling), every interpolated value is wrapped in CoreAr.Isolate, and numerals are western — ArabicOcrText.Clean folds Arabic-Indic and Persian digits before anything is stored, and three tests assert HasArabicIndicDigits is false on messages and on real OCR output. The only technical-looking words are the product names PDF and Word inside FileKindNotAccepted, which is what an office reader would recognise; no codes or paths appear anywhere.

DI AND THE VAULT MOVE. src/Wakeel.UI/Services/Account/VaultStore.cs is deleted and ActivationService uses Wakeel.Core.Services.Documents.VaultStore's static form; UI.Tests and the first-run walkthrough are green. Core registers IDocumentStore, IDocumentService and ILetterDocumentStore as Scoped; the desktop host registers IScanner, IVaultKeyProvider, AddWakeelOcr() and IDerivedDocumentBuilder, closing B3-1b's two unregistered services as ruled. Note for the supervisor: the App.xaml.cs diff also carries lines that are not this package's (ISystemSettingsLauncher, IFileSaveService and the B3-1b letter singletons) — they are another agent's live work in the shared tree, they build, and I left them alone.

VERDICT. One medium finding (a scan that could not be stored still reports success words) is why this is 'fix' rather than 'accept'; the other four are low and could ride along. Nothing outside the package's allowed paths was touched by the builder, no package was added, and I modified no file.
